means: The long-lived computer where your agents work.
Where a dropped computer waits.
Silo's own small program inside a computer.
The edge of a computer.
One way through the boundary.
Everything Silo has written down about a computer: its facts and its reports, written once.
One thing Silo saw itself, from outside the computer. Written once.
One thing a program inside the computer told Silo. Written once. The agent can interfere with it.
What a classifier, or you, think about facts and reports. It can be wrong, and it says whose it is.
Whatever gives an opinion.
A rule is triggered by a fact. It is exact, and it may do anything you wrote in it.
A precaution is triggered by a report or an opinion. It can be wrong, so it takes only protective actions.
Said of an action after which a computer can do something it could not just before.
Said of an action that ends or erases something, and that cannot be undone.
Said of an action that grants nothing and destroys nothing. A wrong one costs only time.
The request waits at the boundary for the answer.
Nothing waits.
One launch of an agent program, and every process descended from it.
A sequence of turns with one model.
One reply of the model in a conversation.
One thing a turn asked for.
What a tool call left behind: processes, file changes, connections.
Said of something that nothing else would bring back if it vanished.
The core piece of Silo. The app, the command line and every tool only talk to it.
